question: Which of the following structures is classified as an accessory organ of digestion?
explanation: The pancreas is an accessory organ that secretes vital enzymes into the gastrointestinal tract through ducts, whereas the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum are parts of the primary alimentary canal. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary function of the accessory organs in the digestive process?

options.A: To provide a continuous muscular tube for food passage
options.B: To absorb all dietary fiber without chemical breakdown
options.C: To contribute vital secretions and enzymes for food breakdown
options.D: To store undigested waste prior to elimination

explanation: Accessory organs contribute vital secretions, enzymes, and biochemical factors to assist in the mechanical and chemical breakdown of food, even though food does not physically pass through them. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which enzyme found in saliva initiates the chemical digestion of complex carbohydrates?
explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) is the primary enzyme in saliva that begins the breakdown of complex carbohydrates in the oral cavity. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h2)

question: What type of salivary output is produced by parasympathetic nervous system stimulation?

options.A: A large volume of watery, enzyme-rich saliva
options.B: A small, viscous volume rich in mucus
options.C: Complete cessation of all salivary flow

explanation: Parasympathetic stimulation specifically triggers the glands to produce a high volume of watery saliva containing digestive enzymes. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which blood vessel transports nutrient-rich, deoxygenated blood directly from the gastrointestinal tract to the liver?
explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries blood laden with absorbed nutrients directly from the GI tract into the liver for processing. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary function of Kupffer cells located within the hepatic sinusoids?

options.C: Producing bile salts for lipid emulsification

explanation: Kupffer cells are specialized phagocytic cells lining the hepatic sinusoids that filter out bacteria and cellular debris from the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary function of bile salts in digestion?

options.A: Chemical breakdown of proteins into amino acids
options.B: Emulsification of large fat globules into smaller micelles
options.C: Neutralization of gastric acid in the stomach

explanation: Bile salts emulsify large dietary fat globules into tiny micelles, increasing the surface area for enzymatic digestion by lipases. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which hormone stimulates the gallbladder to contract and release stored bile into the duodenum?
explanation: Cholecystokinin (CCK) is released in response to dietary fats and proteins, triggering gallbladder contraction and sphincter relaxation. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which cells within the exocrine pancreas are responsible for producing pancreatic juice and digestive enzymes?
explanation: Acinar cells make up the exocrine tissue of the pancreas and secrete the enzymes and alkaline fluid that form pancreatic juice. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of the bicarbonate ions present in pancreatic juice?

options.B: To neutralize acidic chyme entering from the stomach
options.C: To stimulate the release of insulin from beta cells
options.D: To break down complex proteins into amino acids

explanation: Bicarbonate ions neutralize acidic chyme coming from the stomach, establishing an appropriate pH for optimal enzyme activity in the small intestine. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which hormone is primarily released in response to low pH in the duodenum and stimulates bicarbonate-rich fluid secretion?
explanation: Secretin is released when acidic chyme enters the duodenum, signaling the pancreas and liver to secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid to neutralize the acid. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h6)

question: During which phase of digestion is accessory organ secretion most active due to the entry of chyme into the duodenum?
explanation: The intestinal phase is the most active secretory phase, driven by hormones like CCK and secretin released when chyme enters the small intestine. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h6)

question: What pathophysiological mechanism characterizes acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Excessive production of bile salts by the gallbladder
options.B: Premature activation of pancreatic digestive enzymes within the gland
options.C: Hypersecretion of insulin by beta cells leading to hypoglycemia
options.D: Bacterial infection localized exclusively within salivary ducts

explanation: Acute pancreatitis occurs when pancreatic digestive enzymes are prematurely activated inside the pancreas, causing autodigestion and inflammation. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h7)

question: Which clinical finding is commonly associated with impaired liver synthesis of plasma proteins in liver failure?
explanation: Impaired synthesis of albumin by a failing liver reduces plasma oncotic pressure, leading to fluid shifts that cause generalized edema and ascites. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h7)
